possible truth values for the propositions C and D. The truth table reveals that the
premises lead to a contradiction when C is true and D is false. Specifically, if C is true
(T) and D is false (F), ~C is false, making the first premise (~C ⊃ D) true, while the
second premise (D ⊃ C) becomes false since a false antecedent cannot imply a true
consequent. Thus, the argument is invalid. A counterexample is when C is true and D is
false, demonstrating that the premises do not guarantee the conclusion.

The theme of self-sacrifice in the philosophy of Mahasi Sayadaw is intricately linked to
the Buddhist ideals of compassion and the relinquishment of ego for the liberation of all
sentient beings. Mahasi Sayadaw emphasizes the importance of mindfulness and insight
meditation, through which practitioners cultivate a deep understanding of impermanence and
the interconnectedness of all life. This understanding fosters a willingness to engage in
self-sacrifice, as individuals recognize that personal suffering is often intertwined with
the suffering of others. The implications of this theme within Buddhist thought highlight
the transformative power of altruism and the pursuit of enlightenment not solely for
oneself, but as a means to alleviate the collective suffering of humanity. Such self-
sacrifice is not an end in itself, but rather a path leading towards the ultimate
realization of non-self and liberation from the cycle of samsara, thereby reinforcing the
ethical dimensions of Buddhist practice.
answers.explanation: correct because it connects Mahasi Sayadaw's emphasis on mindfulness and insight meditation to the broader Buddhist ideals of compassion and ego relinquishment, illustrating how these concepts foster a willingness to engage in self-sacrifice for the benefit of all sentient beings.
